transcript: In Nia Alikah Robinson's new play at Soho Rep called The Great Privation (How to Flip ten cents into a dollar), two mother-daughter pairs find themselves at the same location, centuries apart. In both timelines, they're played by Crystal Lucas-Perry and Clarissa Vickerie, and as the play progresses, the lines blur between the 1800s and the present day, with the help of some supernatural elements. I thought this play was primarily about the weight of carrying a painful history, but it really integrates a lot of themes such as legacy, faith, and exploitation. For such a dense piece, it is ripe with humor and the dialogue flows really easily. It's not an intimidating watch, and in such an intimate space, I found it near impossible to not be locked in the whole time. The captivating performances and impressive range of all the actors also helped with that. Honestly, I think this is my favorite piece I've seen at Soho Rep up to this point, so I'd put on your radar sooner than later, as it's currently only running through March 23rd. With that, another program for my collection.
